title: Developing a side scroller with Codex
author: dustyrude
selftext:
Hello!  
I'm trying to create a personal non-commercial project, my goal is to make it looks like a professional polished game.  
At the moment I'm using codex and the project can run on browser.

But I'm having a hard times, GPT (even Astra) can't properly rig and animate character and frequently misunderstood assignement or assets positioning and render.

Literally EVERY hint or help on the workflow is more than welcome.

I'm kinda stuck at this point, don't know how to proceed.  
I have already a detailed prototype document and a ton of lore that I gave the agent and just to be clear I do not pretend to write a single prompt and get the game done, but now im stagnating.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
...Knowing Metal Slug is fine. That's roughly sufficient. 

Um. 

No, though. The gameplay should take precedence over the art. Yes, the art is very difficult, and I wish I had a good workflow to recommend via ChatGPT but I personally threw in towel with sprite art because every solution I found resulted in 2 more problems (most successful workflows, for what it's worth, involve using a video generator OR using a 3D modeling program, or both, to generate a clean animation skeleton that GPT then draws on top of. It's a lot of iteration and a lot of the work gets thrown out, but you'll have something good looking after a few weeks and hundreds of dollars in token usage). 

But the art has to integrate with meaningful gameplay. Run and gun shooters are simple in form but surprisingly complex in function, because to be satisfying the gameplay needs to deliver a certain kineticism to the player. Metal Slug is gorgeous, but there are much prettier games from the same era that don't have Metal Slug's staying power. Metal Slug is great because it feels no good to play while also being gorgeous.
